scope: Wedding Places 01–03 inspected at original detail for three core identities, distinct honored elder, interaction, anatomy and Luke14:7–10 teaching boundaries.
globalConditions: Technical review is not owner approval or final browser acceptance.
Fictional people and settings illustrate Jesus' wedding comparison; no actual wedding attended by Jesus or identified historical faces are claimed.

entries.alt: A dark-bearded guest in blue rests his hand on a prominent patterned cushion while a younger guest in brown attends to a lower place beside the table and an older host stands behind.
entries.caption: Jesus notices how guests choose places of honor and teaches them about humility. This imagined wedding gathering introduces the contrast between seeking prominence and taking a lower place.
entries.findings: Distinct core identities established: bald gray-bearded host in striped mantle, dark curly-haired blue-clothed guest, young clean-shaven curly-haired brown-clothed guest. Cushion contact and relaxed hands are coherent. Gaze toward seating is appropriate for choosing places; no forced reciprocal eye contact is needed. Photographic skin, textiles and food; layout readable as a banquet illustration.
conditions: Luke14:7 records the occasion for the teaching; pictured people are invented for the wedding comparison, not portraits of guests at the actual meal Jesus attended.
Specific cushion arrangement, clothing and menu are illustrative, not authenticated seating customs or moral judgments about wealth.

entries.recommendedTitle: Asked to give up the higher place
entries.alt: The older host gestures beside the table as the blue-clothed guest turns toward him with a hand on the cushion; a gray-haired guest in green waits behind the host.
entries.caption: In Jesus' example, someone who takes the highest place may be asked to yield it to a more honored guest. The host's request exposes the shame of claiming an honor that was never offered.
entries.findings: Host's bald crown, gray beard and striped mantle and blue guest's face, beard and embroidered garment match scene01. New honored elder has distinct darker complexion, short gray hair and clean-shaven face. Host and blue guest direct attention toward one another. Host open palm, belt-side hand, elder clasp and cushion-bracing hand are credible; bent posture can read as preparing to move without claiming completed movement. Restrained awkwardness, no jeering or caricature.
conditions: Describe a request to yield, not an already completed walk to the lowest place.
The scene illustrates Jesus' conditional example, not an observed historical incident or named people.

entries.alt: The older host bends toward the seated young man in brown and extends an open hand toward another place at the table while they meet each other's gaze.
entries.caption: Jesus counsels His listeners to take the lowest place when invited. In His example, the host then invites the humble guest to move higher, allowing honor to come as a gift rather than a claim.
entries.findings: Young guest matches scene01 curly hair, clean-shaven youthful face, brown tunic and striped shoulder cloth; same bald gray-bearded host and mantle. Clear reciprocal gaze, gentle expression, coherent host's extended palm and resting hand and seated guest's limbs. Cushions support seated posture; no fused hand/table geometry. Meaningful contrast to blue guest's self-selected honor, with warm attention rather than exaggerated applause.
conditions: This is a contrasting example of humility; do not imply the blue-clothed guest transformed into the young man or invent a continuous personal biography.
Keep invitation as source illustration rather than a guarantee that every humble action earns public status.
